name: Unified Instrument Position Feed
objective: Assemble a single, reconciled position-level feed for the FIS ALM engine covering every on- and off-balance-sheet instrument from Sierra (PIB, T-Bill, FX Forwards) and Symbols/CBS (loans, term deposits, CASA), populating ~260 standardized instrument attributes per position.
problemStatement: ALM, FTP, IFRS 9 and liquidity reporting are each fed from different extracts, so numbers never reconcile and every ALCO cycle starts with spreadsheet stitching. There is no golden position store: instrument classification (fixed/floating, HTM/AFS/HFT), GL tagging and repricing profile are re-derived inconsistently per report.

optimizationTechnique.name: Source-to-PDM Mapping & Golden Position Store
optimizationTechnique.description: The SMX mapping resolves each source record (SYTRANS/IXINST for Sierra, RB_ACCT/RB_TDA/tm_ft_cl_loanbook for CBS) to a FIS PDM instrument entity, applying trade-group and purpose-code filters, join and transformation rules to build one position record reused by all downstream engines.

regulatoryBasis: SBP ALM & IRRBB guidelines; single source of truth for BSD returns
outputs: Golden position record (~260 attributes) per instrument
Fixed / Floating / Non-Maturing / FX classification
HTM / AFS / HFT accounting category
Reconciled asset/liability and ledger tagging

name: Repricing Gap & IRRBB (EVE / NII)
objective: Build the repricing (rate-sensitivity) gap between rate-sensitive assets and liabilities per time bucket, and quantify Interest Rate Risk in the Banking Book through Economic Value of Equity and Net Interest Income sensitivity under SBP-prescribed rate shocks.
problemStatement: The banking book carries a structural mismatch: fixed-rate PIBs and term deposits reprice on different cycles to floating KIBOR-linked advances and administered savings. Without a per-bucket repricing ladder the bank cannot see its EVE exposure or defend NII under +/-100/200/300 bps moves that SBP now expects to be measured.

optimizationTechnique.name: Repricing Ladder + EVE/NII Simulation
optimizationTechnique.description: Each position is slotted into repricing buckets using its next-repricing date (ROLL_DATE for CBS floaters, maturity for fixed). Cashflows are revalued under parallel and non-parallel shocks to derive delta-EVE and 12-month delta-NII, with duration and PV01 by bucket.

regulatoryBasis: Basel IRRBB (BCBS 368); SBP interest-rate risk framework
outputs: Repricing gap ladder (RSA vs RSL, cumulative gap)
Delta-EVE under regulatory rate shocks
12-month Delta-NII at risk
Duration, PV01 and basis-risk view by KIBOR tenor

name: Funds Transfer Pricing Engine
objective: Assign a matched-maturity transfer rate to every asset and liability so business-line margin splits into credit spread, funding/liquidity cost and interest-rate risk, moving all rate and liquidity risk to the central Treasury book.
problemStatement: Branches book both the customer spread and the interest-rate risk, so profitability is overstated for long-tenor lending and understated for stable deposits. With no FTP, capital and pricing decisions are blind to funding cost, and the deposit franchise's true value is invisible.

optimizationTechnique.name: Matched-Maturity FTP Decomposition
optimizationTechnique.description: Each instrument is priced off the KIBOR/PKRV transfer curve at its repricing tenor, then layered with liquidity, funding, credit and option spreads to produce FTP_Coupon_Rate, FTP_Funding_Spread, FTP_Liquidity_Spread, FTP_Credit_Spread and FTP_Option_Spread. Net customer margin = customer rate minus FTP rate.

regulatoryBasis: BCBS FTP principles; internal capital & pricing governance
outputs: Per-deal / product / branch FTP rate and net margin
Funding, liquidity, credit and option spread breakdown
FTP-adjusted NII feed to Customer Profitability Engine
Consistent transfer pricing across conventional & Islamic books

name: Structural Liquidity, LCR & NSFR
objective: Build the contractual and behavioral maturity ladder from instrument cashflows, and compute Basel III LCR and NSFR plus SBP liquidity metrics from the same position and cashflow feed.
problemStatement: Liquidity risk is managed on end-of-day balances, not forward cashflows, so the bank cannot see cumulative funding gaps or stress survival horizon. HQLA, deposit run-off and rollover assumptions live in disconnected spreadsheets, making LCR/NSFR slow and hard to audit.

optimizationTechnique.name: Cashflow Maturity Ladder + Basel Ratios
optimizationTechnique.description: Contractual inflows/outflows are laddered by bucket, overlaid with behavioral run-off for non-maturing deposits and prepayment, then mapped to HQLA levels and Basel weights to compute LCR (HQLA / net 30-day outflows) and NSFR (available / required stable funding).

regulatoryBasis: Basel III LCR & NSFR; SBP liquidity returns
outputs: Daily maturity ladder & cumulative liquidity gap
LCR and NSFR with component breakdown
Core vs volatile deposit split
Contingency funding & survival-horizon view

name: Behavioral Modeling of Non-Maturing Deposits
objective: Model CASA (current and savings) stability, decay and rate sensitivity to separate core from volatile balances and derive the behavioral maturity and repricing profile that contractual data cannot provide.
problemStatement: Current and savings deposits have no contractual maturity, yet they fund the balance sheet. Treating them as overnight overstates liquidity and rate risk; treating them as permanent understates it. Key engine inputs (FTP_AverageBalance, FTP_AverageYield, delivery type) are simply not present in the CBS source.

optimizationTechnique.name: Deposit Decay & Beta Modeling
optimizationTechnique.description: Historical balance and rate series are decomposed into a stable core and a volatile layer with a decay profile; a rate beta captures how administered savings rates track KIBOR. Outputs feed behavioral buckets for liquidity, repricing and FTP.

regulatoryBasis: IRRBB NMD treatment (BCBS 368); SBP behavioral study guidance
inputs: SBP minimum savings rate & policy rate history
Withdrawal / attrition and seasonality (Eid, salary cycles)
outputs: Core vs volatile balance split per product
Behavioral maturity & decay profile
Deposit rate beta (pass-through) for repricing
Behavioral inputs to FTP and liquidity engines

name: Cashflow Generation Engine
objective: Generate contractual and behavioral cashflows for every instrument from its principal amortization, coupon, redemption and early-termination schedules, producing the dated cashflow ladder that feeds liquidity, IRRBB and IFRS 9 EIR calculations.
problemStatement: Cashflow schedules are rebuilt manually each ALM run because payment amounts and dates are frequently absent in source ('Not Required' fields), spread across event tables, and encoded in frequency codes that need FM_PERIOD_FREQ translation. Islamic profit and savings payout conventions are undefined.

optimizationTechnique.name: Schedule Generation from Cashflow Tables
optimizationTechnique.description: Four cashflow tables are populated: AmortizationTable (principal), CouponCashflowTable (interest/profit), RedemptionTable and EarlyTerminationTable. Engine rules generate missing dates/amounts from anchors, frequencies, day-count and business-day conventions and holiday calendars.

inputs: Sierra IXINST_EVT / IXINST_DEF coupon & event schedules
outputs: Principal + interest cashflow schedule per instrument
Behavioral overlays (prepayment, early withdrawal)
Grace periods, stubs and redemption events
Reusable cashflow store for all downstream engines

name: HTM / AFS / HFT Classification & Fair Value
objective: Classify securities by accounting intent (HTM, AFS, HFT) from Sierra trade-group and purpose codes to drive amortized-cost vs fair-value measurement, capture clean/dirty market value and support AFS reserve and hedge-accounting movements.
problemStatement: The same PIB or T-Bill is measured differently depending on its book (HTM at amortized cost, AFS at FVOCI, HFT at FVTPL), but classification and valuation basis are handled manually. Price basis (clean vs dirty, price vs yield from IXINST_MKM) and book value from GLTRDAMORT are inconsistently applied.

optimizationTechnique.name: Classification Rules + Mark-to-Market
optimizationTechnique.description: Trade-group/purpose codes (HMLB/HTMB, ASLB/ASMB, TBILL, PIB) map to accounting category. IXINST_MKM mid price/yield gives clean and dirty market value; GLTRDAMORT gives amortized cost; the difference drives the AFS reserve and P&L.

regulatoryBasis: IFRS 9 classification & measurement; SBP investment classification
outputs: Accounting category (HTM / AFS / HFT) per security
Clean & dirty market value, unrealized gain/loss
AFS reserve movement and hedge-accounting entries
Auditable instrument-to-ledger reconciliation

name: IFRS 9 ECL Integration
objective: Stage every exposure (IFRS 9 Stage 1/2/3), attach PD/LGD/CCF risk parameters and compute Expected Credit Loss on the same instrument-level cashflows used for ALM, reconciling provisions to the GL and aligning with SBP and Basel asset classes.
problemStatement: ECL is computed in a separate risk system on a different exposure snapshot than ALM, so staging, EAD and cashflows never tie out. Past-due data is held at loan-number level and must be spread to drawdown/position level, and PIT-vs-TTC PD calibration lacks governance.

optimizationTechnique.name: Staged ECL on Shared Cashflows
optimizationTechnique.description: The ALM position feed carries CD_CreditQualityStage, CD_DaysPastDueStage and rating; exposures are staged, then PD (PIT & TTC), lifetime PD, LGD and CCF are applied to the shared cashflow ladder discounted at EIR to produce 12-month and lifetime ECL and loss allowance.

regulatoryBasis: IFRS 9 impairment; SBP classification & provisioning; Basel asset class
inputs: ALM position feed with CD_* dimensions & TotalPastDueAmount
CBS loan status flags & past-due buckets; RB_OD_REPOSITORY
outputs: IFRS 9 stage per exposure (1 / 2 / 3)
12-month & lifetime ECL and loss allowance
Provision coverage reconciled to GL
Shared PD/LGD for Basel RWA & risk-based pricing
